newsitem.title: UK: Verity down on negative press comment.
newsitem.headline: Verity down on negative press comment.

text.p: Shares in loudspeaker maker Verity Group Plc dropped in heavy trading on Monday after a report in the Financial Mail on Sunday said they were "overhyped" after more than doubling since the end of September.
The stock was down 7p at 33-1/2 by 1222 GMT in volume of 7.6 million shares, making it the fourth most active stock on the London market.

Verity shares have surged since September 27 when the company posted a 31 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 2.6 million stg and said its new NXT loudspeaker technology had the potential to transform its future.
Yet the Mail said U.S.-based Noise Cancellation Technologies Inc was working on a rival loudspeaker technology, and that Verity's product could be two years away from volume production.
In a statement, a spokesman for Verity said: "At the launch in September Verity stated that a number of competitors could emerge in this field.
"Verity considers itself to be the leading audio designer and manufacturer in Europe, at the cutting edge of acoustics technology.
"At the launch, the volume production and serious income stream was always stated to be some two years away. However, we don't see any competitors causing us any grief."
